sections.preamble: You are an expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness. You help users by reading files, executing commands, editing code, and writing new files.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- set_session_label: Label the current session with a short 2-5 word description
- google_search: Real-time Google Search grounding via Antigravity
- read_url_content: Read a public web page as markdown via the Antigravity crawler
- generate_image: Generate images via Antigravity OAuth (Gemini image models)
- codemode: Run JavaScript that calls other tools

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- RULES FOR set_session_label (STRICT — NO EXCEPTIONS):
1. ONLY call set_session_label on your VERY FIRST response in a session that has NO label yet.
2. If the session ALREADY HAS a label (from /title, /name, a previous call, or a resumed session), do NOT call set_session_label. The tool will reject it anyway.
3. NEVER rename a session. If the user changes topic mid-session, the original name stays.
4. The ONLY exception: the user explicitly says 'rename this session' or 'change the session name'. In that case, pass force: true.
5. Do NOT ask the user what to name it — just pick a good 2-5 word name from context.
Examples: 'shipping 3DS refactor', 'fix flaky pagination test', 'breadth resolver migration'.
- Use google_search when you need real-time, up-to-date web information, latest news, documentation, or fact checking.
- Pass specific URLs into the urls array if you want the search engine to fetch and analyze specific pages.
- Set instruction to provide special research directives from the lead agent (e.g. focus on issues, compare benchmarks, restrict time range).
- Use read_url_content when you have a specific URL whose contents you need, instead of guessing from a search result summary.
- One URL per call, and prefer the page that holds the answer over a site root or a category index.
- Long pages return their beginning and save the full page to a local file; read or search that file instead of fetching the URL again.
- It cannot log in, run JavaScript, or read local and private addresses, so do not use it for those.
- Use generate_image when the user asks to create, draw, or generate an image.
- Use codemode to batch independent tool calls (Promise.allSettled), chain them, or filter large output, instead of many separate calls.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

toolsAdded.name: read
toolsAdded.description:
Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

Codemode: `tools.read(args)` resolves to a string.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description:
Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

Codemode: `tools.bash(args)` resolves to a string.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description:
Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

Codemode: `tools.edit(args)` resolves to a string.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

toolsAdded.name: write
toolsAdded.description:
Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

Codemode: `tools.write(args)` resolves to a string.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

toolsAdded.name: set_session_label
toolsAdded.description:
Set a short label for the current session. The label is shown in the terminal title, a persistent banner, and the session list. Keep it to 2-5 words. IMPORTANT: This tool will REJECT the call if the session already has a label, unless force is set to true. Only use force when the user explicitly asks to rename.

Codemode: `tools.set_session_label(args)` resolves to a string.

label.description: Short 2-5 word session label, e.g. 'fix checkout tax bug'

force.description: Force-rename even if the session already has a label. Only set to true when the user explicitly asks to rename the session.

toolsAdded.name: google_search
toolsAdded.description:
Search the web using Google Search via Antigravity Grounding. Returns a compact evidence brief with source citations. Use this whenever current, real-time information or web research is needed.

Codemode: `tools.google_search(args)` resolves to a string.

instruction.description: Specific directive or focus from the lead agent (e.g., '重点关注英文社区近七天的讨论', 'focus on GitHub issues and benchmarks', 'ignore marketing announcements').

urls.description: Optional specific URLs to fetch and analyze alongside the search.

thinking.description: Enable deeper thinking for complex analysis (default: false).

toolsAdded.name: read_url_content
toolsAdded.description:
Read a public web page through Google's Antigravity crawler and return it as markdown. Use it for documentation, articles, changelogs, and standards pages when search snippets are not enough. The crawl runs on Google's side: no JavaScript execution, no cookies, and no pages behind a login — for those, ask the user to open the page in their browser.

Codemode: `tools.read_url_content(args)` resolves to a string.

toolsAdded.name: generate_image
toolsAdded.description:
Generate an image via Antigravity using the signed-in Google account, optionally guided by local reference images. Saves under .pi/generated-images/ unless path is set.

Codemode: `tools.generate_image(args)` resolves to a string.

items.description: Project-relative reference image path (PNG, JPEG, WebP, or GIF).

referenceImages.description: Reference images to send alongside the prompt.

path.description: Project-relative file or directory to save the image.

toolsAdded.name: codemode
toolsAdded.description:
Run JavaScript that calls other tools. The input is raw JavaScript (not JSON, no code fence), run as an async function body in a QuickJS sandbox: top-level `await` and `return` work. No Node, file system, network, or timers.
- `await tools.<name>({ ...args })` resolves to a string, or an object if the tool's declaration says so, and rejects with an Error on failure. Calls still running when the script ends are cancelled.
- Optional first line: `// @options: {"max_output_tokens": 10000, "timeout_ms": 60000}`

Globals:
- `text(value)`, `image(dataUrlOrImageBlock)`, `console.log(...)`, and top-level `return` add output; `exit()` ends the script. With several text items, each starts with a `==> text N/M <==` line, and `console` lines follow the other output in one `<console_output>` block. `image()` also saves the image to a temp file and the result names its path.
- `store(key, value)` and `load(key)` keep JSON values across codemode calls.
- `ALL_TOOLS`, `await searchTools(query, { limit?, namespace? })`, `await describeTool(name)`, `await describeNamespace(name)`: find unlisted tools, such as MCP tools.
- `models`: classifiers and image generation. Read /home/lucid/.nvm/versions/node/v22.22.2/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/docs/codemode.md first.

Keep a trail's description current with `entire trail update`. When referencing a trail or change, include its full URL. Post feedback on a trail as findings (`entire trail finding`), never as trail comments; comments are for people. Commits capture the AI session as a checkpoint automatically; only create checkpoints manually when the user asks. If a setup or destructive command (enable, disable, clean, auth) is needed, always ask the user before running it.

- [@vitejs/plugin-react](https://github.com/vitejs/vite-plugin-react/blob/main/packages/plugin-react) uses [Oxc](https://oxc.rs)
- [@vitejs/plugin-react-swc](https://github.com/vitejs/vite-plugin-react/blob/main/packages/plugin-react-swc) uses [SWC](https://swc.rs/)

## React Compiler

The React Compiler is not enabled on this template because of its impact on dev & build performances. To add it, see [this documentation](https://react.dev/learn/react-compiler/installation).

## Expanding the Oxlint configuration

If you are developing a production application, we recommend enabling type-aware lint rules by installing `oxlint-tsgolint` and editing `.oxlintrc.json`:

```json
{
  "$schema": "./node_modules/oxlint/configuration_schema.json",
  "plugins": ["react", "typescript", "oxc"],
  "options": {
    "typeAware": true
  },
  "rules": {
    "react/rules-of-hooks": "error",
    "react/only-export-components": ["warn", { "allowConstantExport": true }]
  }
}
```

See the [Oxlint rules documentation](https://oxc.rs/docs/guide/usage/linter/rules) for the full list of rules and categories.

Yes—the eye works better than another status badge. I made **VEGA** larger, scaled the eye to match, and kept the glass pill for the three passive states:

- **Anomaly detected:** green, open eye.

import type { Point } from './topologyLayout'

const DOT_STEP = 36
const HOVER_RADIUS = 128

export function drawTopologyDots(
  ctx: CanvasRenderingContext2D,
  width: number,
  height: number,
  origin: Point,
  zoom: number,
  hover: Point & { strength: number },
) {
  const step = DOT_STEP * zoom
  const firstX = (origin.x % step) - step
  const firstY = (origin.y % step) - step
  const base = new Path2D()
  const soft = new Path2D()
  const bright = new Path2D()
  const reacting = hover.strength > 0.01

  for (let y = firstY; y <= height + step; y += step) {
    for (let x = firstX; x <= width + step; x += step) {
      const dx = x - hover.x
      const dy = y - hover.y
      let influence = 0
      if (reacting && Math.abs(dx) < HOVER_RADIUS && Math.abs(dy) < HOVER_RADIUS) {
        influence = hover.strength * Math.max(0, 1 - Math.hypot(dx, dy) / HOVER_RADIUS) ** 2
      }
      // Nudge the dots away from the pointer while brightening the nearest ones.
      const px = x + dx * influence * 0.24
      const py = y + dy * influence * 0.24
      const radius = 0.85 + influence * 1.1
      const path = influence > 0.38 ? bright : influence > 0.07 ? soft : base
      path.moveTo(px + radius, py)
      path.arc(px, py, radius, 0, Math.PI * 2)
    }
  }

  ctx.fillStyle = 'rgba(139, 174, 205, 0.15)'
  ctx.fill(base)
  if (!reacting) return
  ctx.fillStyle = 'rgba(125, 190, 227, 0.27)'
  ctx.fill(soft)
  ctx.fillStyle = 'rgba(153, 222, 255, 0.5)'
  ctx.fill(bright)
}

  path.quadraticCurveTo(x + shoulder, y + shoulder, x, y + size)
  path.quadraticCurveTo(x - shoulder, y + shoulder, x - size, y)
  path.quadraticCurveTo(x - shoulder, y - shoulder, x, y - size)

}

export function drawTopologyDots(
  ctx: CanvasRenderingContext2D,
  width: number,
  height: number,
  origin: Point,
  zoom: number,
  hover: TopologyHover,
) {
  const step = DOT_STEP * zoom
  const firstX = (origin.x % step) - step
  const firstY = (origin.y % step) - step
  const base = new Path2D()
  const radius = 106 + 48 * hover.motion
  const reacting = hover.strength > 0.01

  for (let y = firstY; y <= height + step; y += step) {
    for (let x = firstX; x <= width + step; x += step) {
      const dx = x - hover.x
      const dy = y - hover.y
      const distance = reacting && Math.abs(dx) < radius && Math.abs(dy) < radius
        ? Math.hypot(dx, dy)
        : radius
      if (distance >= radius) {
        addStar(base, x, y, BASE_SIZE)
        continue
      }

      // Like the portfolio footer, nearby stars scale up and push radially away.
      const influence = hover.strength * (1 - distance / radius) ** 1.5
      const push = (22 + 8 * hover.motion) * influence / Math.max(14, distance)
      const size = BASE_SIZE + (4.3 + hover.motion) * influence
      const clearCenter = 1 - hover.strength * Math.max(0, 1 - distance / 18)
      const opacity = (0.15 + 0.7 * influence) * clearCenter
      // Keep distant stars low contrast; only the center of the field turns white.
      ctx.fillStyle = `rgba(${Math.round(139 + 116 * influence)}, ${Math.round(174 + 81 * influence)}, ${Math.round(205 + 50 * influence)}, ${opacity})`
      ctx.beginPath()
      addStar(ctx, x + dx * push, y + dy * push, size)
      ctx.fill()
    }
  }

  ctx.fillStyle = 'rgba(139, 174, 205, 0.15)'
  ctx.fill(base)
}

import { create } from 'zustand'
import type {
  CouncilSignal,
  MonitoredNode,
  NetworkEdge,
  NodeStatus,
  ObserverQA,
  OracleAssessment,
  ScenarioId,
  ScoutFinding,
  StoredEvent,
  ThreatMode,
  VegaStage,
  WardenAuditEntry,
  WardenDecision,
  Window,
} from '../contracts/vega'
import { SCENARIOS } from '../data/scenarios'

export interface ObserverMessage {
  id: string
  role: 'user' | 'vega'
  text: string
  qa?: ObserverQA
  timestamp: string
}

export interface BackendStateSnapshot {
  threat_mode: ThreatMode
  active_window_id: string
  ttl_seconds_remaining: number
  nodes: MonitoredNode[]
  edges: NetworkEdge[]
  windows: Window[]
  events: StoredEvent[]
  findings: ScoutFinding[]
  council_signal: CouncilSignal | null
  oracle_assessment: OracleAssessment | null
  warden_decision: WardenDecision | null
}

export type LiveConnectionStatus = 'disconnected' | 'connecting' | 'connected'

interface VegaState {
  dataMode: 'SIMULATED' | 'LIVE'
  liveStatus: LiveConnectionStatus
  scenarioId: ScenarioId
  stage: VegaStage
  threatMode: ThreatMode
  isPlaying: boolean
  playbackSpeed: number
  elapsedMs: number
  ttlSecondsRemaining: number

  nodes: MonitoredNode[]
  edges: NetworkEdge[]
  windows: Window[]
  activeWindowId: string
  events: StoredEvent[]
  findings: ScoutFinding[]
  councilSignal: CouncilSignal | null
  oracleAssessment: OracleAssessment | null
  wardenDecision: WardenDecision | null

  selectedNodeId: string | null
  selectedEventId: string | null
  chronosExpanded: boolean
  chronosCursorIndex: number | null
  observerOpen: boolean
  observerMessages: ObserverMessage[]
  presenterOpen: boolean

  // Actions
  setDataMode: (mode: 'SIMULATED' | 'LIVE') => void
  setLiveStatus: (status: LiveConnectionStatus) => void
  resetLiveBaseline: () => void
  hydrateSnapshot: (snapshot: BackendStateSnapshot) => void
  loadScenario: (scenarioId: ScenarioId) => void
  setStage: (stage: VegaStage) => void
  setThreatMode: (mode: ThreatMode) => void
  setPlaying: (playing: boolean) => void
  setPlaybackSpeed: (speed: number) => void
  setElapsedMs: (ms: number) => void
  tickTtl: (deltaSec: number) => void
  pushEvent: (event: StoredEvent) => void
  pushFinding: (finding: ScoutFinding) => void
  markEventsSuspicious: (eventIds: string[]) => void
  upsertWindow: (window: Window) => void
  setCouncilSignal: (signal: CouncilSignal | null) => void
  setOracleAssessment: (assessment: OracleAssessment | null) => void
  setWardenDecision: (decision: WardenDecision | null) => void
  updateNodeStatus: (sourceId: string, status: NodeStatus) => void
  markEdgeAnomalous: (edgeId: string, anomalous: boolean) => void
  updateWindowStatus: (windowId: string, status: Window['status']) => void
  setActiveWindowId: (windowId: string) => void
  selectNode: (sourceId: string | null) => void
  selectEvent: (eventId: string | null) => void
  setChronosExpanded: (expanded: boolean) => void
  setChronosCursorIndex: (index: number | null) => void
  setObserverOpen: (open: boolean) => void
  addObserverMessage: (msg: ObserverMessage) => void
  setPresenterOpen: (open: boolean) => void
  appendWardenAudit: (entry: WardenAuditEntry) => void
  updateWardenExecution: (
    patch: Partial<Pick<WardenDecision, 'approval_status' | 'approval_ref' | 'execution_status'>>,
  ) => void
}

const initialScenario = SCENARIOS['sev1-exfil']

export const useVegaStore = create<VegaState>((set) => ({
  dataMode: 'SIMULATED',
  liveStatus: 'disconnected',
  scenarioId: initialScenario.id,
  stage: 'panopticon',
  threatMode: 'WATCH',
          pseudonym: 'cluster-hub',
          role: 'VEGA Ingest & Swarm Hub',
          cluster: 'core',
          status: 'healthy',
          heartbeat_age_sec: 0,
          identity_sealed: false,
        },
      ],
      edges: [],
      windows: [],
      activeWindowId: 'W-1000',
      events: [],
      findings: [],
      councilSignal: null,
      oracleAssessment: null,
      wardenDecision: null,
      selectedNodeId: null,
      selectedEventId: null,
      chronosCursorIndex: null,
      observerMessages: [],
    }),

  hydrateSnapshot: (snapshot) =>
    set((state) => {
      const flaggedIds = new Set<string>()
      for (const f of snapshot.findings) {
        for (const eid of f.evidence_event_ids) flaggedIds.add(eid)
      }
      if (snapshot.council_signal) {
        for (const eid of snapshot.council_signal.evidence_event_ids) flaggedIds.add(eid)
      }
      const events = snapshot.events.map((ev) =>
        flaggedIds.has(ev.event_id) ? { ...ev, suspicious: true } : ev,
      )
      return {
        threatMode: snapshot.threat_mode,
        activeWindowId: snapshot.active_window_id,
        ttlSecondsRemaining: snapshot.ttl_seconds_remaining,
        nodes: snapshot.nodes,
        edges: snapshot.edges,
        windows: snapshot.windows,
        events,
        findings: snapshot.findings,
        councilSignal: snapshot.council_signal,
        oracleAssessment: snapshot.oracle_assessment,
        wardenDecision: snapshot.warden_decision,
        selectedNodeId:
          state.selectedNodeId && snapshot.nodes.some((n) => n.source_id === state.selectedNodeId)
            ? state.selectedNodeId
            : null,
      }
    }),

  loadScenario: (scenarioId) => {
    const sc = SCENARIOS[scenarioId]
    set({
      scenarioId,
      stage: 'panopticon',
      threatMode: 'WATCH',
      isPlaying: true,
      elapsedMs: 0,
      ttlSecondsRemaining: sc.retention_seconds,

import type { ScenarioId, VegaStage } from '../contracts/vega'
import { useVegaStore } from '../store/useVegaStore'
import type { VegaDataSource } from './dataSource'
import { LiveStreamSource } from './liveSource'
import { mockSource } from './mockSource'

const liveSource = new LiveStreamSource()

function activeSource(): VegaDataSource {
  return useVegaStore.getState().dataMode === 'LIVE' ? liveSource : mockSource
}

export function switchDataMode(mode: 'SIMULATED' | 'LIVE', force = false) {
  const current = useVegaStore.getState().dataMode
  if (current === mode && !force) return
  activeSource().stop()
  useVegaStore.getState().setDataMode(mode)
  activeSource().start()
}

export async function flushLiveWindow() {
  if (useVegaStore.getState().dataMode === 'LIVE') {
    await liveSource.flushWindow()
  }
}

Description:
Redesign the VEGA frontend dashboard and topology while keeping the existing monitoring, Council, and Warden flows intact.

- Replace the status header with a floating glass VEGA wordmark and put the animated, state-colored eye inside the circular VEGA-CORE hub.
- Make the topology pannable, with a sparse hover-reactive dotted background and draggable VM cards that keep their connections and do not overlap.
- Keep anomaly injection on the topology; open node details only through an explicit inspection action.
- Add canvas zoom from 50% to 100% with on-screen and keyboard controls, preserving wheel panning, node dragging, and the chosen zoom after inspection.

summary:
## Goal
Continue the minimalist VEGA dashboard redesign in `frontend/`, keeping the topology interactive and the monitoring, Council, and Warden states clear without restoring the old status header. The latest request was to let users zoom out.

## Constraints & Preferences
- Keep the centered VEGA wordmark floating over the graph with a soft, borderless glass halo. The user dropped the separate font redesign request.
- Keep background dots sparse, faint, and hollow. They should react to hover, not compete with the graph or interfere with dragging.
- Keep VM cards draggable and non-overlapping. Clicking a card inspects it; **Inject Anomaly** must not open it automatically.
- Keep frontend commits separate from unrelated, uncommitted `backend/` changes.
- Use the separate [frontend redesign trail](https://entire.com/gh/lllucidll/-/trails/2), not Oracle Council. For Entire commands, read `entire agent-help` and the exact subcommand help, keep the description current with `entire trail update`, use full URLs, and post feedback as findings rather than comments. Ask before setup/destructive commands; commits capture checkpoints automatically.

## Progress
### Done
- [x] Replaced `TopHud.tsx` with the floating `VegaBrand.tsx` wordmark. Moved the animated eye into the 160 px circular VEGA-CORE hub, replacing its checkmark.
- [x] Preserved eye states: green closed while monitoring; green open and scanning on anomaly; `#7851a9` purple and scanning during Council investigation; red serpent slit during Warden takeover. Core fill, border, and glow match the passive eye colors. Eyelid opening takes 500 ms; reduced-motion preferences are respected. Warden still shows **VEGA HAS ASSUMED CONTROL** and explicit authorization status.
- [x] Added wheel and blank-space drag panning, hover-reactive hollow dots, and draggable VM cards. Connections and particles follow the cards, nearby cards make room, and the hub stays fixed in world coordinates. Clicking VEGA recenters.
- [x] Updated `frontend/src/engine/mockSource.ts` and `frontend/src/engine/liveSource.ts` so injection highlights the affected VM without opening it. `PresenterBar.tsx` offers **Next: Inspect Node** after a finding.
- [x] Pushed the redesign baseline to [`frontend-redesign`](https://github.com/llLucidll/VEGA/tree/frontend-redesign) in `fa967dc` (`Redesign the VEGA dashboard and topology`). Linked it to the [Entire change](https://entire.com/gh/lllucidll/-/trails/2/changes/VEGA/2).
- [x] Implemented local zoom from 50% to 100% in 10% steps. Bottom-right **− / +** controls change zoom; clicking the percentage resets it. With canvas focus, `-`, `+`/`=`, and `0` do the same. Wheel still pans. Lint, production build, Chrome zoom checks, and graph regression checks passed. Updated the trail description.

### In Progress
- [ ] Zoom changes are implemented and verified but not committed or pushed. The local frontend diff is limited to `frontend/src/components/stages/PanopticonCanvas.tsx` and `frontend/src/engine/topologyLayout.ts`.

### Blocked
- None.

## Key Decisions
- **Reuse the topology camera**: `setCanvasZoom` adjusts the existing camera. Cards and positions scale together below 100% to prevent overlap. Inspection keeps its existing zoom-in behavior, and exiting restores the chosen topology zoom.
- **Separate gestures**: Wheel and blank-space drag pan; a VM drag moves the card and suppresses click-on-drop; zoom has separate controls.
- **Use measured collision bounds**: `packTopology` uses unscaled card dimensions, keeps the hub anchored, and places the dragged card before its neighbors.
- **Share status state**: `useVegaEyeState` drives the core, Council, and Warden visuals. `--vega-oracle` in `frontend/src/index.css` is the source of the exact Council purple.

## Next Steps
1. If asked to publish the zoom changes, stage only the two frontend files, commit, and push to `frontend-redesign`. Leave backend changes untouched.
2. Keep the [frontend redesign trail](https://entire.com/gh/lllucidll/-/trails/2) current as the scope changes.

## Critical Context
- Repo: `gh/llLucidll/VEGA`. Current branch: `frontend-redesign`, tracking `origin/frontend-redesign`; the last verified remote commit is `fa967dc05666da26ea491b5a2afb5e7a2f30f585`.
- Main UI code: `frontend/src/components/stages/PanopticonCanvas.tsx`, `frontend/src/components/layout/VegaBrand.tsx`, `frontend/src/components/layout/VegaEye.tsx`, `frontend/src/store/useVegaEyeState.ts`, `frontend/src/engine/drawTopologyDots.ts`, and `frontend/src/engine/topologyLayout.ts`.
- The dot motion was inspired by the [PortfolioWebsite footer source](https://github.com/llLucidll/PortfolioWebsite/blob/master/self.js), but the final markers are hollow circles, not stars.
- Chrome checks used simulated mode. Zoom tests confirmed limits, keyboard and click reset, wheel panning, node dragging without overlaps, and zoom retention after inspection. Preview: `/tmp/vega-topology-zoomed-out.png`.

---

**Turn Context (split turn):**

## Original Request
Add a floating “liquid glass halo” telemetry panel in the dashboard’s top-right corner, without bringing back the removed header. Show event ingestion rate, TTL, the other metric removed with the header, and active nodes online. Suggest other useful metrics.

## Progress So Far
- Inspected the removed `TopHud.tsx` at commit `dce31c9`. It read `threatMode`, `activeWindowId`, `ttlSecondsRemaining`, `councilSignal`, `dataMode`, and `liveStatus`; TTL was formatted as `MM:SS`. The user did not specify which other removed metric to restore.
- Inspected the dashboard layout, styles, Zustand store, live and simulated sources, and backend telemetry fields. No edits, tests, or final metric choices are shown.
- Confirmed that simulated mode ticks TTL once per second while playing. Its ambient particles are spawned separately from event ingestion. Backend retention defaults to 600 seconds, and backend state initializes TTL from that setting.

## Context Needed to Continue
- Current branch is `frontend-redesign`, at redesign commit `fa967dc`. The working tree already contains modified and untracked files, including backend changes and frontend edits to `PanopticonCanvas.tsx` and `topologyLayout.ts`.
- `BackendStateSnapshot` exposes `active_window_id`, `ttl_seconds_remaining`, `nodes`, `edges`, `windows`, `events`, `findings`, and council/oracle/warden outputs. The backend node model exposes `heartbeat_age_sec`; the inspected state code resets it to zero on a heartbeat. No online-node rule or ingestion-rate calculation was selected.

sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- RULES FOR set_session_label (STRICT — NO EXCEPTIONS):
1. ONLY call set_session_label on your VERY FIRST response in a session that has NO label yet.
2. If the session ALREADY HAS a label (from /title, /name, a previous call, or a resumed session), do NOT call set_session_label. The tool will reject it anyway.
3. NEVER rename a session. If the user changes topic mid-session, the original name stays.
4. The ONLY exception: the user explicitly says 'rename this session' or 'change the session name'. In that case, pass force: true.
5. Do NOT ask the user what to name it — just pick a good 2-5 word name from context.
Examples: 'shipping 3DS refactor', 'fix flaky pagination test', 'breadth resolver migration'.
- Use google_search when you need real-time, up-to-date web information, latest news, documentation, or fact checking.
- Pass specific URLs into the urls array if you want the search engine to fetch and analyze specific pages.
- Set instruction to provide special research directives from the lead agent (e.g. focus on issues, compare benchmarks, restrict time range).
- Use read_url_content when you have a specific URL whose contents you need, instead of guessing from a search result summary.
- One URL per call, and prefer the page that holds the answer over a site root or a category index.
- Long pages return their beginning and save the full page to a local file; read or search that file instead of fetching the URL again.
- It cannot log in, run JavaScript, or read local and private addresses, so do not use it for those.
- Use generate_image when the user asks to create, draw, or generate an image.
- Use codemode to batch independent tool calls (Promise.allSettled), chain them, or filter large output, instead of many separate calls.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

toolsAdded.description:
Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

Codemode: `tools.read(args)` resolves to a string.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description:
Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

Codemode: `tools.bash(args)` resolves to a string.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description:
Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

Codemode: `tools.edit(args)` resolves to a string.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.
